program: In-home youth and family therapy, foster care and parent recovery support
priceScope: Matched FY2025 full annual recipient cost against partial MST family-treatment benefits; other channels unknown, not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Savio provides home-based youth and family therapy with public-service funding and coordination.
The matched 2025 reference uses 520 MST clients, not a sum of overlapping statewide programs.
It assesses clinical health and signed caregiver resources without assigning children's future wages.
strengths: Newest IRS native MST count and full annual expenses are matched to 2025.
Home-based family work offers a concrete clinical and access mechanism.
Multiple program counts, broad annual reach and public-funded savings are not added as independent benefits.
reservations: Causal completion, utility, alternative-provider additionality and local residence remain hypotheses.
Full recipient cost covers foster care, early childhood, trauma and grant administration whose effects are unknown.
Near-free family care is not equivalent to cash savings or donor-funded marginal capacity.

sections.what: Current home-based services include adolescent family treatment, trauma care, early-childhood caregiver work, foster care and parent substance recovery. Historical residential care closed in 2020 and is not counted as current adolescent capacity. New Bluestem family recovery is a separate current mechanism, not a reason to revive the old adolescent residential program.
sections.monitoring: Request deduplicated MST households, completed treatment and fidelity, comparable outcomes against contracted alternatives, caregiver disposable resources, Denver resident share and demonstrable unrestricted-donation capacity. Separate program substitution from treatment received and outcomes gained.
sections.qualitative: FY2025 original reports 520 MST clients plus FFT, sexual-behavior, trauma, family-wellness and foster cohorts; cross-program overlap is unknown, so they are not summed. The annual 1,800 Colorado families reached is not completed unique therapy. Public Medicaid/CYMHTA/county funding and other clinicians form the counterfactual. Broad success narratives do not identify causal QALYs.
sections.cost: FY2025 full IRS cost $14,274,461 is paired with 520 MST clients. The annual report's $13,906,047 expense differs; no unexplained blending is used. Household conversion .9, completed dose .8, incremental additionality .25, response .4, utility .04 for one year and CBSA share .55 are judgments, not observed causal coefficients. Caregiver $250 net resources are after taxes, benefits withdrawn, childcare and work costs, require completed care and separate .5 resource success, and are not child wages. Positive resource gains receive .5 overlap discount; all exposed families retain $30 time/access cost and .0002 process harm regardless of benefit. Actual otherwise-paid copay and external payer losses are central zero judgments with full-incidence sensitivity. The $7,093,017 adolescent mixed-program cost tests the recognized cost boundary; it is not allocated MST-only or marginal-gift cost.
sections.funding: Current giving page identifies Savio House Inc. DBA Savio, EIN 84-0570279, Stripe processing and greatest-need giving unless restricted. No transaction was made. Statewide contracts and Medicaid support can substitute for donated funding; government expenditure or retail free therapy value is not automatically net family consumption. New program needs indicate possible uses, not measured next-dollar impact.

model.costScope: Full calendar FY2025 IRS functional expense; netted event expenses blank. Only partial MST benefit reference; other channels unknown.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .55 share of MST client households inside ten-county Denver CBSA19740. Statewide programs and Colorado Springs/Western Slope reach prevent assigning all beneficiaries to Denver.
model.formula: Health = (N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − full exposed harm) × local share. Completed eligible households jointly log net caregiver resources and full home-session costs; all negatives and distinct payer incidence retained. Price = 10 × C / combined health and income equivalents.
model.counterfactual: County/Medicaid contracted care, other family treatment and justice services without Savio; home access and fidelity may differ.
model.attribution: Judged .25 incremental additionality against publicly funded substitute providers, completion .8 and response .4. Native enrollment is not causal outcome.
model.uncertainty: Clinical utility, duration, completion, family overlap, actual substitute provision, caregiver gain, local share and next-gift capacity unmeasured. Other programs unknown, not zero.
model.nativeOutcomes: Original FY2025 reports 520 MST clients, not completed households; other native program categories are not added.
